The problem with people is we tend to think if some of something is good, more of something is better. So we hear something like eat less = good and it equates in our minds to eat none = better. Your body needs energy to keep running. It's annoying but you have to continually put energy in to get peak performance out. You try to run thru an entire tank of gas in the time an engine is made to run thru a 7th of a tank and it'll destroy the engine thru overheating and probably weld various parts together. This is what you're suggesting to do to your body. So if the goal here is to lose weight, you have a small amount of work to do. You can do it without any exercise at all if you so choose. But first you have to figure out how many calories you need in a day. Now you heard a million times the next step is to then eat less than that, but there's a bit more to it. You want to eat around 10% less if you're in decent shape and want to lose, around 30% less if you're not in decent shape. Gong more than 35-40% less than what you need in a given day is a really bad idea. It is NOT "better". It is attempting to run the engine on fumes. It will stall. It will sputter. All around bad time had by all. Tryin to eat more than 30% less than what you need for more than a week is a bad idea. Throw in 1 day at like 50 calories more than you need and then go back to the 30% deficit. Body builders who have had nutrition down for decades do 3 days of the deficit with 1 day over. And just go back and forth 3 days and 1 day. But if you're just looking to lose as much as possible as quick as possible, the max you would do without fear of drastic medical conditions is 7 days. All of this information is available if you look for it. Obviously you haven't and probably won't. Just don't do this kind of thing for extended period of time. The time frame you hear the most is 6 weeks. Do like a month of a calorie deficit and then like a week of eating at your calorie needs amount just to like give your body a chance to adjust. Also be sure to redo the math on how much you need as you lose. Good Luck!
